The literarily-inclinded daughter of a physicist  and an epidemiologist, Lowry was forced to find her own way toward normal through an upbringing that was anything but.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Nothing But Capers
Staff Comment: When his wife set out to write her magnum opus cookbook, food critic Stackhouse thought the hardest part would be making sure he didn't outgrow his favorite slacks. He never expected that amidst the thyme and roux and cleavers, their relationship would be tried, tested, and ultimately perfected. Tastefully seasoned with the recipes that brought them to the brink, "Nothing But Capers" follows the tumult that strained then saved his marriage and his life.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

No More Lightning
Staff Comment: Beloved author Charles Fenimore strikes out in a new direction with his first graphic novel. In this devestating tale of daring, ingenuity, and just a dash of  luck, Fenimore dmonstrates his genius for combining visual flare and cutting prose. Uchon's mechanical contraption to tame lightning brings its own threats to her tinder-box community stricken by wildfires. Will Uchon's luck run out on the eve of the biggest lightning storm to threaten the sleepy town of Delanro in decades?

Title: Inconvenient Confessions: a memoir
Staff Comment: Lowry's comedic genius shines through every moment of her memoir. Told with clear eyes and biting wit, the anecdotes of each chapter bring to life a world of eccentric academics. Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

In this devestating tale of daring, ingenuity, and just a dash of  luck, Fenimore dmonstrates his genius for combining visual flare and cutting prose. Title: Inconvenient Confessions: a memoir
Staff Comment: Lowry's comedic genius shines through every moment of her memoir. Told with clear eyes and biting wit, the anecdotes of each chapter bring to life a world of eccentric academics. The literarily-inclinded daughter of a physicist  and an epidemiologist, Lowry was forced to find her own way toward normal through an upbringing that was anything but.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

the life and times of an utterly inconsequential person
Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Staff Comment: Beloved author Charles Fenimore strikes out in a new direction with his first graphic novel. In this devestating tale of daring, ingenuity, and just a dash of  luck, Fenimore dmonstrates his genius for combining visual flare and cutting prose. Uchon's mechanical contraption to tame lightning brings its own threats to her tinder-box community stricken by wildfires. Will Uchon's luck run out on the eve of the biggest lightning storm to threaten the sleepy town of Delanro in decades?

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Who Did You Think You Were Kidding?
Staff Comment: Antrim's ability to make you laugh through your tears has never been stronger than in his memoirs. Diagnosed with terminal cancer at 38, Antrim reflects back on his life with the grace and wisdom of a man twice his age. "Who Did You Think You Were Kidding" reminds us that even on a sad path toward a death far too soon, the journey is what matters.

Title: Nothing But Capers
Staff Comment: When his wife set out to write her magnum opus cookbook, food critic Stackhouse thought the hardest part would be making sure he didn't outgrow his favorite slacks. He never expected that amidst the thyme and roux and cleavers, their relationship would be tried, tested, and ultimately perfected. Tastefully seasoned with the recipes that brought them to the brink, "Nothing But Capers" follows the tumult that strained then saved his marriage and his life.

Staff Comment: Antrim's ability to make you laugh through your tears has never been stronger than in his memoirs. Staff Comment: Lowry's comedic genius shines through every moment of her memoir. Told with clear eyes and biting wit, the anecdotes of each chapter bring to life a world of eccentric academics. Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Who Did You Think You Were Kidding?
Staff Comment: Antrim's ability to make you laugh through your tears has never been stronger than in his memoirs. Diagnosed with terminal cancer at 38, Antrim reflects back on his life with the grace and wisdom of a man twice his age. "Who Did You Think You Were Kidding" reminds us that even on a sad path toward a death far too soon, the journey is what matters.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Tastefully seasoned with the recipes that brought them to the brink, "Nothing But Capers" follows the tumult that strained then saved his marriage and his life.

Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Who Did You Think You Were Kidding?
Staff Comment: Antrim's ability to make you laugh through your tears has never been stronger than in his memoirs. Diagnosed with terminal cancer at 38, Antrim reflects back on his life with the grace and wisdom of a man twice his age. "Who Did You Think You Were Kidding" reminds us that even on a sad path toward a death far too soon, the journey is what matters.

Title: Inconvenient Confessions: a memoir
Staff Comment: Lowry's comedic genius shines through every moment of her memoir. Told with clear eyes and biting wit, the anecdotes of each chapter bring to life a world of eccentric academics. The literarily-inclinded daughter of a physicist  and an epidemiologist, Lowry was forced to find her own way toward normal through an upbringing that was anything but.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Staff Comment: Beloved author Charles Fenimore strikes out in a new direction with his first graphic novel. In this devestating tale of daring, ingenuity, and just a dash of  luck, Fenimore dmonstrates his genius for combining visual flare and cutting prose. Uchon's mechanical contraption to tame lightning brings its own threats to her tinder-box community stricken by wildfires. Will Uchon's luck run out on the eve of the biggest lightning storm to threaten the sleepy town of Delanro in decades?

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Who Did You Think You Were Kidding?
Staff Comment: Antrim's ability to make you laugh through your tears has never been stronger than in his memoirs. Diagnosed with terminal cancer at 38, Antrim reflects back on his life with the grace and wisdom of a man twice his age. "Who Did You Think You Were Kidding" reminds us that even on a sad path toward a death far too soon, the journey is what matters.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Turn Left Til You Get There
Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Who Did You Think You Were Kidding?
Staff Comment: Antrim's ability to make you laugh through your tears has never been stronger than in his memoirs. Diagnosed with terminal cancer at 38, Antrim reflects back on his life with the grace and wisdom of a man twice his age. "Who Did You Think You Were Kidding" reminds us that even on a sad path toward a death far too soon, the journey is what matters.

Title: Nothing But Capers
Staff Comment: When his wife set out to write her magnum opus cookbook, food critic Stackhouse thought the hardest part would be making sure he didn't outgrow his favorite slacks. He never expected that amidst the thyme and roux and cleavers, their relationship would be tried, tested, and ultimately perfected. Tastefully seasoned with the recipes that brought them to the brink, "Nothing But Capers" follows the tumult that strained then saved his marriage and his life.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Staff Comment: When his wife set out to write her magnum opus cookbook, food critic Stackhouse thought the hardest part would be making sure he didn't outgrow his favorite slacks. He never expected that amidst the thyme and roux and cleavers, their relationship would be tried, tested, and ultimately perfected. Tastefully seasoned with the recipes that brought them to the brink, "Nothing But Capers" follows the tumult that strained then saved his marriage and his life.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Inconvenient Confessions: a memoir
Staff Comment: Lowry's comedic genius shines through every moment of her memoir. Told with clear eyes and biting wit, the anecdotes of each chapter bring to life a world of eccentric academics. The literarily-inclinded daughter of a physicist  and an epidemiologist, Lowry was forced to find her own way toward normal through an upbringing that was anything but.

Title: Who Did You Think You Were Kidding?
Staff Comment: Antrim's ability to make you laugh through your tears has never been stronger than in his memoirs. Diagnosed with terminal cancer at 38, Antrim reflects back on his life with the grace and wisdom of a man twice his age. "Who Did You Think You Were Kidding" reminds us that even on a sad path toward a death far too soon, the journey is what matters.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Say it with Snap!

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Turn Left Til You Get There
Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Staff Comment: Beloved author Charles Fenimore strikes out in a new direction with his first graphic novel. In this devestating tale of daring, ingenuity, and just a dash of  luck, Fenimore dmonstrates his genius for combining visual flare and cutting prose. Uchon's mechanical contraption to tame lightning brings its own threats to her tinder-box community stricken by wildfires. Will Uchon's luck run out on the eve of the biggest lightning storm to threaten the sleepy town of Delanro in decades?

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Title: No More Lightning
Staff Comment: Beloved author Charles Fenimore strikes out in a new direction with his first graphic novel. In this devestating tale of daring, ingenuity, and just a dash of  luck, Fenimore dmonstrates his genius for combining visual flare and cutting prose. Uchon's mechanical contraption to tame lightning brings its own threats to her tinder-box community stricken by wildfires. Will Uchon's luck run out on the eve of the biggest lightning storm to threaten the sleepy town of Delanro in decades?

Title: Inconvenient Confessions: a memoir
Staff Comment: Lowry's comedic genius shines through every moment of her memoir. Told with clear eyes and biting wit, the anecdotes of each chapter bring to life a world of eccentric academics. The literarily-inclinded daughter of a physicist  and an epidemiologist, Lowry was forced to find her own way toward normal through an upbringing that was anything but.

Title: Hashtag QuokkaSelfie
Staff Comment: #QuokkaSelfie took the internet by storm in the early 21s. These adorable marsupials, quickly dubbed "the happiest animal on Earth" became an internet sensation when tourists started posting selfies with the smiling mammals. Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.

Rottnest Island, once an Australian Aboriginal penal colony, transformed into an eco-tourism destination thanks to these picture-perfect smiling creatures. But even beaming quokkas can't escape the darker side of intense human attention. Reports began circulating of quokkas being kicked liked footballs. Instagram labeled #QuokkaSelfie as potentially violating animal welfare. Conservationists decried "lumpy jaw", a potentially fatal infection caused by bread fed to these herbivores from human hands. In this—ultimately hopeful—exploration of #QuokkaSelfie, Langston Lippman and colleagues take a deeper look at the phenomenon of celebrating nature to the brink of destroying it.
